title: Al-Mu'min, the Giver of Security
hookLine: the Giver of Security and Faith, and a heart that lives between fear and hope
tomorrow: secure in Him. but who's awake while you sleep?

cards: Lock the door. Check the lock. Check it again.
A body can be safe while a heart still doesn't believe it.
After Peace in Surah al-Hashr comes Al-Mu'min, which Pickthall translates the Keeper of Faith; scholars explain it as the Giver of Security, the one who makes safe and keeps faith.
So, yesterday's question: what makes a heart feel safe? Inside the tradition, the answers pull two ways.

teach.b: One verse says: don't lose hope. In Pickthall's words, from Surah az-Zumar: Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins. And a sacred hadith in Bukhari says, in paraphrase: I am as My servant thinks of Me.
Another verse warns the other way.
In Surah al-A'raf, in paraphrase, only people who are lost feel secure from Allah's plan.
So some scholars said: let fear lead while you're healthy and strong, so you don't grow careless, and let hope lead near the end.
Others said hope should lead, because Allah is the Giver of Security, and despair is a wrong of its own. Here's each side's best case.

The fear side: a heart that feels completely safe stops checking itself, and the Qur'an warns about exactly that. The hope side: a heart that's always afraid can't love, and the Qur'an says despair not.
Some held both, with an image some scholars used: fear and hope are a bird's two wings, and it needs both to fly.
And the name holds both too. Al-Mu'min gives security; mu'min is also the everyday word for a believer, someone who trusts.
Something to tell a friend tonight: one Arabic word names Allah and names the person who trusts Him.

how: Muslim teachers often describe faith as living between fear and hope (khawf and raja'), and many Muslims turn to verses like 'despair not of the mercy of Allah' when afraid.

o: the One who tests how strong faith is
the first person ever to believe in Islam
the Giver of Security, who makes safe

games.q: between fear and hope — tap the pairs.
p: don't feel secure from His plan

s: the Qur'an only ever tells believers to feel safe
it says despair not, and it also warns about feeling secure from Allah's plan.
mu'min names both Allah and a believer
Al-Mu'min is a name of Allah; mu'min is also the everyday word for someone who trusts.

games.q: your friend says faith should mostly feel like hope. you lean toward a healthy fear. what's your friend's best case?
o: the Qur'an says despair not; a heart that's always afraid can't love.
fear is outdated; people today don't need it in religion at all.
hope means nothing you do matters, so there's no reason to worry.
games.why: despair not of the mercy of Allah, and I am as My servant thinks of Me: that's the hope side's strongest ground.

practice: Think of one person who might be anxious this week. Send them one plain line that makes them feel safer: I've got you, or I'll be there Thursday, whatever's true. For the sit, rest a hand on your chest and let your own breath slow.

wordCard.voice: Al-Mu'min: the Giver of Security and Faith, the one who makes safe. The same word, mu'min, names a believer.

orig.note: Arabic: the Giver of Security and Faith; the same word, mu'min, means a believer.

carryVoice: Hold this close: secure in him, between fear and hope, both wings working. Talk tomorrow.
